title: Changes of State
description: Heating and cooling can change matter from one state to another. Melting, freezing, evaporating, and condensing are all changes of state.

exercises.question: What happens when you HEAT ice?
exercises.exp: Heating ice makes it melt — it changes from solid to liquid water.

exercises.question: What is it called when liquid water changes to ice?
exercises.exp: Freezing happens when a liquid cools and becomes a solid — like water turning to ice.

exercises.question: What causes water to EVAPORATE?
exercises.exp: Heat makes liquid water evaporate — it turns into water vapour (a gas)!

exercises.question: When steam touches a cold window it becomes water drops. This is called ___.
exercises.exp: Condensing happens when gas cools and becomes liquid. You see it on cold windows!

exercises.question: Chocolate melts in the sun. What change has happened?
exercises.exp: Melting changes a solid to a liquid. Chocolate is solid until it gets warm.

exercises.question: Which process is the OPPOSITE of melting?
exercises.exp: Freezing is the opposite of melting — liquid becomes solid when cooled.

exercises.question: You heat water in a pot. Bubbles form and steam rises. What is happening?
exercises.exp: Boiling is fast evaporation! Water turns to water vapour (steam).

exercises.question: On a cold morning, you can see your breath. Your warm breath is ___ when it hits cold air.
exercises.exp: Warm water vapour in your breath condenses into tiny droplets you can see in cold air.

exercises.question: Which needs COOLING to happen?
exercises.exp: Freezing needs cooling — water must cool below 0°C to turn into ice.

exercises.question: A puddle dries up on a sunny day because the water ___.
exercises.exp: The sun heats the puddle water and it evaporates into the air.

exercises.question: What change happens when candle wax melts?
exercises.exp: Wax is solid until the candle flame heats it. Then it melts — solid to liquid!

exercises.question: When liquid water changes to water vapour it is called ___.
exercises.exp: Evaporation changes liquid to gas. Wet clothes dry because water evaporates.

exercises.question: Ice cubes in a drink cool the drink down. What is the ice doing?
choices: melting and absorbing heat from the drink, cooling it
exercises.exp: Ice melts by absorbing heat from the warmer drink — this is why drinks get cold with ice!

exercises.question: What is the change of state: liquid → solid?
exercises.exp: Freezing changes liquid to solid by removing heat. Water → ice is the classic example.

exercises.question: What is the change of state: gas → liquid?
exercises.exp: Condensing changes gas to liquid. Steam on a cold mirror condenses into water drops.

exercises.question: Why do wet swimming clothes DRY in the sun?
choices: the sun's heat evaporates the water into the air
the clothes absorb the water back
exercises.exp: The sun's heat energy evaporates water from wet clothes — the liquid water turns to water vapour and escapes into the air.

exercises.question: Butter left on a hot pan melts quickly. Which two things are needed for melting?
choices: heat energy and the material must be a solid first
exercises.exp: Melting needs heat energy applied to a solid. The pan's heat melts the solid butter into liquid.

exercises.question: The outside of a cold can of juice has water drops on it. This is because ___.
choices: water vapour in the warm air condenses on the cold surface
the can is sweating inside out
exercises.exp: Warm air holds water vapour. When it touches the cold can, the vapour condenses into liquid droplets!

exercises.question: Which of these is an example of EVAPORATION in daily life?
choices: a wet mop drying on the floor
water turning to ice in winter
exercises.exp: A wet mop dries because the liquid water evaporates into the air — liquid becoming gas!

exercises.question: What happens to the MASS of water when it freezes into ice?
exercises.exp: Mass is conserved during a change of state — the same amount of water is there, just in a different state.

exercises.question: Steam is water in the ___ state.
exercises.exp: Steam is water vapour — water in its gas state. It forms when water boils at 100°C.

exercises.question: Which change of state happens when you make ice lollies (popsicles) in the freezer?
exercises.exp: Juice in the moulds loses heat in the freezer and freezes solid — liquid juice becomes solid ice lolly!

exercises.question: Heating and cooling are ___ to each other.
exercises.exp: Heating adds energy and cooling removes energy — they are opposite processes that reverse each other.

exercises.question: Why does a puddle DISAPPEAR faster on a hot sunny day than a cool cloudy day?
exercises.exp: More heat energy means water evaporates faster. A hot sunny day gives puddles much more energy to evaporate!

exercises.question: Which of the four changes of state ADDS heat to the surroundings?
exercises.exp: Freezing releases heat to the surroundings as particles lock into place. The other three require heat to be added.

exercises.question: A glass of water is left uncovered for a week. The water level drops. Why?
choices: evaporation — water slowly turns to vapour and escapes
gravity pushed water into the table
exercises.exp: Even at room temperature, water slowly evaporates — the level drops as molecules escape into the air.

exercises.question: Snow is ___.
choices: frozen rain (water that freezes as it falls)
a mixture of water and air
exercises.exp: Snow forms when water vapour freezes directly into ice crystals in clouds and falls as snowflakes!

exercises.question: Which best describes CONDENSATION happening?
choices: cold juice glass getting wet on the outside on a humid day
exercises.exp: Water vapour from the air condenses on the cold glass surface — the glass feels wet even though it is not leaking!

exercises.question: The water cycle involves many changes of state. Which correctly matches the step to the change?
choices: water rising as vapour from the ocean = condensation
exercises.exp: Clouds form when water vapour rises, cools, and CONDENSES into tiny water droplets. That step is condensation!

exercises.question: You heat an ice cube gently. List the changes of state in order.
exercises.exp: Ice (solid) → melts to liquid water → if heated more, evaporates to water vapour (gas). Melting then evaporating!

exercises.question: Which change of state is REVERSED by adding heat?
exercises.exp: Condensation (gas → liquid) is reversed by adding heat, which causes evaporation (liquid → gas) again.

exercises.question: Ice melting and water freezing are ___.
choices: opposite processes that reverse each other
exercises.exp: Melting (adding heat, solid→liquid) and freezing (removing heat, liquid→solid) are perfectly opposite and reversible!

exercises.question: Water evaporates from a lake and forms clouds. In the clouds, it ___.
exercises.exp: Water vapour rises into cool air and condenses — forming the billions of tiny droplets that make up clouds.

exercises.question: When does water boil?
exercises.exp: Pure water boils at 100°C (212°F) at sea level — this is when it rapidly turns from liquid to gas (steam).

exercises.question: When does water freeze?
exercises.exp: Pure water freezes at 0°C (32°F) — this is when it changes from liquid to solid (ice).

exercises.question: Dew on grass in the morning is caused by ___.
choices: water vapour in the air condensing on cool surfaces overnight
exercises.exp: Overnight, air cools and water vapour condenses on grass and leaves — forming tiny dew drops by morning!

exercises.question: Which of these involves EVAPORATION?
choices: ice cubes forming in a tray
wet clothes drying on a washing line
exercises.exp: Wet clothes dry because liquid water evaporates — it absorbs heat and turns into water vapour in the air.

exercises.question: Why does a lake SHRINK in very hot, dry weather?
choices: the water freezes at the bottom
water evaporates faster than rain replaces it
exercises.exp: Hot weather speeds up evaporation. If more water evaporates than falls as rain, the lake gets smaller over time.

exercises.question: Frost on a window is frozen ___.
choices: water vapour that turned directly from gas to solid
exercises.exp: Frost can form when water vapour freezes directly on a cold surface, or when condensed droplets freeze. Both are ice!

exercises.question: Which change of state is happening when you breathe on a cold mirror and it fogs up?
exercises.exp: Your warm breath contains water vapour. When it hits the cold mirror, it condenses into tiny water droplets — fog!

exercises.question: Salt dissolves in water. When the water evaporates, the salt ___.
choices: is left behind as solid crystals
exercises.exp: Salt cannot evaporate — only water does. When the water evaporates, solid salt crystals are left behind. Salt remains!

exercises.question: A change of state is a PHYSICAL change because ___.
choices: the material changes to a completely different substance
no new substance is made — only the arrangement of particles changes
exercises.exp: In changes of state, NO new substance is created. Ice, water, and steam are all H₂O — just in different states.

exercises.question: Which of these does NOT involve a change of state?
exercises.exp: Cooking an egg is a CHEMICAL change — new proteins form. The others are physical changes of state (water/ice/steam).

exercises.question: What do we call the temperature at which a substance melts?
exercises.exp: The melting point is the exact temperature at which a solid turns to liquid. For ice it is 0°C.

exercises.question: Candle wax melts when heated and hardens when cooled. These changes are ___.
choices: physical and reversible — same wax, different states
exercises.exp: Candle wax melting and re-solidifying is a reversible physical change — it is the same wax throughout!

exercises.question: The WATER CYCLE is powered mainly by ___.
exercises.exp: The sun's energy evaporates water from oceans and lakes, driving the whole water cycle — clouds, rain, and back again!

exercises.question: When you see your breath on a cold day, it is water vapour ___.
choices: condensing into tiny droplets in the cold air
exercises.exp: Warm humid air from your lungs meets cold outside air and water vapour condenses into a visible white cloud!

exercises.question: Which of these is an example of FREEZING in everyday life?
choices: ice cream melting in the sun
making ice cubes in the freezer
wet hair drying in the breeze
exercises.exp: Making ice cubes means cooling liquid water until it freezes solid — a perfect example of freezing!

exercises.question: Why do you put ICE in a drink to keep it cold?
choices: as ice melts, it ABSORBS heat from the drink and cools it
ice releases heat into the drink
exercises.exp: Melting requires energy (heat). Ice absorbs heat from the drink to melt — this is what cools your drink down!

exercises.question: What name is given to the change from liquid to gas at the SURFACE of a liquid (not boiling)?
exercises.exp: Evaporation happens at the surface of a liquid at any temperature — not just at the boiling point.

exercises.question: Snow on a mountain slowly disappears on a sunny day even when the temperature stays BELOW 0°C. This is ___.
choices: sublimation — solid ice turns directly to water vapour
exercises.exp: Sublimation! Snow can turn directly into water vapour (gas) without becoming liquid first — especially at altitude!
